Administration is requesting Board approval of a Transportation Coordination License and Services Agreement between the Grandview C-4 School District and HopSkipDrive, Inc. HopSkipDrive is a student transportation coordination provider that facilitates transportation services for students through a network of vetted drivers and transportation partners. The agreement provides the District with an additional transportation option to support student attendance, access to educational programs, McKinney-Vento services, foster care transportation needs, special program transportation, and other circumstances where traditional transportation options may not be available or practical.

The agreement will be effective from March 19, 2026, through March 19, 2027, with the option for annual renewal upon mutual agreement of both parties. Either party may terminate the agreement with thirty (30) days written notice. Under the agreement, HopSkipDrive will provide transportation coordination services through its platform and maintain required insurance coverage, including automobile liability, general liability, sexual misconduct and molestation coverage, and employer liability insurance. The agreement also includes FERPA compliance provisions, background check requirements for individuals providing services, and student data privacy protections.

Transportation services will be utilized on an as-needed basis. Costs are based on a fee structure that includes a base fare, mileage rate, and any applicable additional services. There is no minimum service commitment required by the District.

Approve of the Transportation Coordination License and Services Agreement between Grandview C-4 School District and HopSkipDrive, Inc. to provide supplemental student transportation services as outlined in the agreement.

As the district's reliance on instructional and operational technology continues to grow, additional support is needed to ensure timely technical assistance, device management, infrastructure maintenance, and customer service for staff and students. The Technology Assistant position will provide first-level technical support and assist in maintaining district technology resources across all buildings and departments.


The Technology Assistant will provide technical support to district staff and students by assisting with the installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of technology equipment and software. The position will support the district's technology infrastructure and help ensure reliable access to instructional and operational technology resources.

Primary responsibilities include:

 

  • Providing first-level technical support for hardware, software, and network-related issues.
  • Assisting the deployment, maintenance, and inventory management of district technology devices
  • Supporting network infrastructure, user account management, and technology security procedures.
  • Assisting with technology projects, upgrades and district initiatives.
  • Providing customer service and technology support to staff, students, and families.
Approve the creation and posting of the Technology Assistant position as presented.
Salary and benefits will be funded through the district's approved technology and operational budgets.  (Salary/Benefits range from $40,000-$50,000)

The Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act was signed into law by President Obama on December 13, 2010.  One of the provisions of the legislation mandates that school nutrition programs move towards charging paid meal category students at a price that is on average equal to the difference between free meal reimbursement and paid meal reimbursement.  Schools that charge less than this amount are required to gradually increase their prices over time until they meet the requirement. Attachment 1 shares historical Grandview meal prices.

 

We are recommending a 10-cent increase to all breakfast and lunch meal prices for the 2026-2027 school year, which would result in the following prices:

Title: c. Grandview Education Foundation revised MOU

fields.Content:
The Grandview Education Foundation was formed in 1997 with a mission to partner with the Grandview C-4 School District and the community to enhance educational opportunities for students and staff in the district.  Throughout their history, they have been able to provide numerous scholarships for our students and educational grants for our teachers. 

 

A Memorandum of Understanding with GEF was approved by the Board of Education in 2022 for a three-year term to provide ongoing support for day-to-day operations and an increased ability to raise funding.   As outlined in the 2022 MOU, the District received quarterly reports regarding the progress toward achieving stated goals related to increased fundraising, participation, and number of grants/scholarships offered.  After review of this data, the District recommended and the Board approved a new three year MOU for the same $40,000.00 per year amount. After reviewing data and discussions between the District and GEF, it was determined that an additional amount was warranted due to meeting all goals outlined and new fundraising goals established by the Foundation. The administration recommends revising the remaining years of the MOU with the Education Foundation for a total yearly amount of $50,000.00 per year (an additional $10,000.00 per year)  to continue supporting them in their mission.
Approve revising the current MOU with the Grandview Education Foundation for an amount not to exceed $50,000.00 per year for the remaining two years.

During the 2016-17 school year, the Grandview C-4 School District began conducting safety and security screenings at all secondary school sites.  The screenings began in response to incidents in our schools involving weapons, which compromised the safety of our students and staff.  Those incidents, along with ongoing national-level school safety concerns, continue to result in the need for increased levels of security measures in our schools. The screenings include the use of a metal detector wand and process that is similar to what is used at sporting event venues.  Our screening process is designed to minimize the amount of time students are out of the classroom and continue to be supported by our District safety committee.

Since they began, the screenings that have been conducted at all secondary schools have been successful in confiscating weapons and other unauthorized items that either should not be at school or should be announced to staff, such as prescription medication. This process has led to a decrease in the number of unauthorized items brought into the school overall.   The screening process continues to be improved and is supported by our District safety committee. In order to maintain an ongoing safe and secure environment for all students and staff, the district and site administration recommend the continuing practice of conducting security screenings throughout the school year at both the high school and middle school levels.

In order to maintain an ongoing safe and secure environment for all students and staff, the district and site administration recommend the continuing practice of conducting security screenings throughout the school year at both the high school and middle school levels.
Approve the continuing practice of conducting security screenings throughout the 2026-27 school year at the secondary school sites.

Over the past year, district administration has reviewed attendance and truancy practices to improve the collection, accuracy, and analysis of student attendance data. This work included collaboration among district staff, review of state attendance requirements, examination of best practices, and consultation with neighboring school districts. The goal has been to strengthen systems that support student attendance, improve communication with families, and provide timely interventions when attendance concerns arise.

The presentation will provide the Board of Education with an overview of:

  • Historical attendance and chronic absenteeism trends at the state and national levels.
  • Missouri attendance laws and district policy requirements.
  • Grandview C-4 attendance data and current attendance trends.
  • A tiered attendance intervention framework designed to provide increasing levels of support and accountability for students and families.
  • Staff roles and responsibilities related to attendance monitoring and intervention.
  • Research connecting attendance to student achievement and long-tern student success.
  • Future planning efforts, including community partnerships and enhanced intervention strategies.
Approve this as informational only.

The Missouri Career Development and Teacher Excellence Plan, commonly known as the Career Ladder Program, is a voluntary performance-based compensation initiative established by state statute. It aims to provide salary supplements to teachers who undertake additional responsibilities and voluntary efforts beyond their contractual obligations. The program is designed to recognize and reward teacher excellence, thereby promoting higher retention rates and enhancing student outcomes.  

The Grandview C-4 School Board approved the implementation of this program on April 17, 2025 after a year-long planning process by District administration and a teacher committee.  This group will provide an update on this program, the successes achieved in year one, and what the 2026 school year will look like for the program.
Accept this update as informational.

The proposed plan will replace our buses at about a 10-year life cycle while vans will be closer to the 15-year mark. Approve a five-year transportation fleet replacement plan as shown on attachments 1&2.
